checks: Parallel translation of any proper containing cap to its boundary at y only reduces mass. A pure-base normal retains each boundary fiber in full and has mass at least α. A whole-space cap has mass M. Each nonvertical cap has a unit continuous normal and a closed atomic trace t_z≤0 of weight at least α.

An infimizing equality sequence is eventually nonvertical because 0<γ_d<1 and α>0. Compactness of the sphere and the finite product of extended lines, with a constant trace chosen by finiteness of P, supplies one subsequence. With finite cutoffs, convergence of cap indicators holds except on a d-null ordinary hyperplane. The ±∞ cases are respectively empty and full for all late terms by boundedness, with no bounded-base-normal assumption.

Every retained site has limiting cutoff ≤0 and limiting cap mass at least γ_d w_z. A negative finite cutoff adds positive volume in the centered interior ball, and −∞ gives full mass. Equality thus forces trace weight α, zero retained cutoffs, and ordinary equality for every retained site with the same u. For an excluded site the limiting mass is zero, so its cutoff is +∞ or at least the strictly positive support value. A strictly smaller cutoff cuts an open set since a support maximizer can be moved toward the interior centroid.

For any nonempty minimal face, including a singleton and the full hull, relative interior gives a representation of y with strictly positive coefficients on every face mark by averaging the individual representations. Both affine displacement sums vanish, so the same cutoff sum is zero at every sequence index. An omitted face site would give a positive lower bound on that sum for all late indices. A proper face has weight at least α by a closed exposing halfspace, including for lower-dimensional hulls. The full face has weight M. Positivity then identifies the trace with exactly the face sites.

An affine graph projection identifies the minimal faces and turns any containing ambient cap trace into a containing base halfspace trace or the whole graph. The proposed converse cap passes through y. On a proper face the affine penalty vanishes there and a finite R chosen strictly beyond all off-face support ratios excludes every off-face fiber. On the full face no penalty is needed. This also covers a singleton base, d=1 and the case α=M.
